# Cris Santos Company | Manufacturing | Mid-Market

> Cris Santos Company, Inc. is a privately held mid-market company with 850 employees, operating as a connected medical device manufacturer (electromedical equipment).

This folder is a self-contained scenario. Read this page first, then open any project folder (P01-P10). Each project folder has a `_context.md` explaining what that deliverable looks like for this company.

## At a glance
| | |
|---|---|
| Legal name | Cris Santos Company, Inc. |
| Legal form | Privately held corporation |
| Ownership | Private equity-backed; board with an audit committee |
| Employees | 850 employees |
| Size tier | Mid-Market: Business that exceeds the SBA size standard for its primary NAICS industry and has fewer than 1,000 employees |
| SBA size status | Small (SBA standard for NAICS 334510: 1,250 employees; 13 CFR 121.201) |
| Primary industry | NAICS 334510 Electromedical and Electrotherapeutic Apparatus Manufacturing |
| Vertical | Manufacturing (NAICS sector 31-33) |
| Primary system | Device software development and manufacturing systems (PLM and MES) |
| IT footprint | Multi-cloud or hybrid with on-premises systems, several business applications, dedicated security tooling |
| Who owns security and compliance | Security manager or vCISO, a small GRC function, internal audit co-sourced |

> **Sizing note:** The SBA standard for this industry is 1,250 employees, so a company with fewer than 1,000 employees still qualifies as small. This scenario is sized at 500-999 employees (Census SUSB class) per the tier rule and remains SBA-small.

## What the business handles
- **Sensitive data:** Device design files and source code; SBOMs and vulnerability data; export-controlled technical data (EAR/ITAR where applicable); patient data received from devices in service (may be PHI when handled for a covered entity)
- **Critical systems:** MES; ERP / PLM; DCS / PLCs / robotics; SCADA and historians; Quality/LIMS; CAD/CAM and CNC networks

## Who regulates it
Department of Defense (DFARS/CMMC, DCSA); Department of State DDTC (ITAR); Department of Commerce BIS (EAR, ICTS); FDA (medical device cybersecurity, food facilities); CISA (Chemical & Critical Manufacturing SRMA)

| Requirement | Citation | Size thresholds / exemptions |
|---|---|---|
| [DFARS 252.204-7012 Safeguarding Covered Defense Information and Cyber Incident Reporting](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-48/section-252.204-7012) | 48 CFR 252.204-7012 (MAY 2024) | No small-business exemption; flowdown required to subcontracts involving CDI/operationally critical support, including commercial products/services. |
| [CMMC Program rule (32 CFR Part 170) + DFARS CMMC acquisition rule (DFARS 252.204-7021)](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2025/09/10/2025-17359/defense-federal-acquisition-regulation-supplement-assessing-contractor-implementation-of) | 32 CFR Part 170 (FR Doc. 2024-22905, Oct. 15, 2024); 48 CFR 204.75 and 252.204-7021 (NOV 2025) (FR Doc. 2025-17359, Sep. 10, 2025, DFARS Case 2019-D041) | No size exemption. Applies to solicitations/contracts above the micro-purchase threshold, except those exclusively for COTS items (32 CFR 170.3(c)). Level set by DoD per contract (FCI -> L1; CUI -> L2; high-priority CUI -> L3). Conditional status valid 180 days; final L1 1 year, L2/L3 3 years. |
| [ITAR (International Traffic in Arms Regulations)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-22/chapter-I/subchapter-M) | 22 CFR Parts 120-130 (registration 22 CFR 122.1; encrypted-data carve-out 22 CFR 120.54(a)(5)) | No size threshold; one occasion of manufacturing/exporting triggers registration. |
| [EAR (Export Administration Regulations)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-15/subtitle-B/chapter-VII/subchapter-C) | 15 CFR Parts 730-774 (encrypted-data carve-out 15 CFR 734.18(a)(5)) | No size threshold. |
| [FD&C Act sec. 524B cyber device requirements](https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-prelim-title21-section360n-2&num=0&edition=prelim) | 21 U.S.C. 360n-2 | None. |

Whether each requirement applies at this size is decided in P03 (gap analysis), step 1.

## The 10 projects for this company
| # | Project | What it covers here |
|---|---|---|
| P01 | [Risk Register](P01_risk-register/_context.md) | Enterprise and system-level registers. 40-60 risks; semi-quantitative; risk appetite statements. |
| P02 | [System Security Plan (SSP)](P02_system-security-plan/_context.md) | A major system (Moderate impact). Full SSP with baseline tailoring and inherited controls. System: Device software development and manufacturing systems (PLM and MES). |
| P03 | [Regulatory Gap Analysis](P03_regulatory-gap-analysis/_context.md) | All applicable regulations for the primary business line. Requirement-level; evidence sampling. Regulation: FD&C Act section 524B (cyber devices). |

| P05 | [Business Impact Analysis (BIA)](P05_business-impact-analysis/_context.md) | All business units and processes. Quantified impact (financial; operational; regulatory). |
| P06 | [Security Policy Set](P06_security-policies/_context.md) | 5 policies plus supporting standards. Policies plus standards for key domains. |
| P07 | [Security Control Assessment](P07_control-assessment/_context.md) | 25-40 controls. Independent-style assessment with sampling. |
| P08 | [Incident Response Runbook](P08_incident-response-runbook/_context.md) | Two incident types. Runbooks integrated with crisis management and legal. Incident: Exploited vulnerability in a fielded connected medical device. |
| P09 | [SOC 2 Readiness Checklist](P09_soc2-readiness/_context.md) | All relevant categories. Readiness assessment for a Type 2 audit. |
| P10 | [AI Governance Risk Assessment](P10_ai-governance/_context.md) | AI use-case portfolio. Inventory; risk tiering; model risk controls. AI use case: AI-enabled device software function (image analysis). |
